title: stream-resume-and-idempotency-protocol-for-multi-region-failover
creator: Liam O'Connor
body:
Summary:
Design and implement a protocol and SDK primitives to safely resume streaming inference requests across region failovers while maintaining deduplication guarantees for mutating and non-mutating endpoints. Current retry and idempotency mechanisms in the platform assume request/response parity; streaming inference introduces ordering and partial-output semantics that can cause duplicated tokens, partial state re-application, or stuck circuits during multi-region failover. This ticket defines: 1) an opaque resume token and versioned idempotency header format, 2) server-side resume semantics for streaming and chunked responses, 3) SDK surface changes and migration strategy, and 4) operational telemetry and rollback plan.

Goals:
- Provide a way for clients to resume an interrupted streaming response from an equivalent model replica in another region without producing duplicate permanent side-effects or breaking ordering-sensitive applications.
- Keep client-side changes minimal: new headers + resume primitive in SDKs.
- Ensure backward compatibility: existing non-upgraded clients continue to work with best-effort semantics.
- Integrate with existing circuit-breaker, hedging, and load-shedding rules so resume attempts obey SLO-driven backoff and do not amplify load.

Non-goals:
- Strong transactional exactly-once across arbitrary customer-side state changes (out of scope).
- Rewriting existing persistent storage semantics for customer workloads.

Design overview:
- Idempotency model: classify endpoints as MUTATING or NON_MUTATING. Mutating endpoints (e.g., long-running document edits that commit state) require stricter guarantees: idempotency-key + server-assigned resume_token. Non-mutating endpoints (pure text generation with no server-side commits) may use best-effort resume.
- Headers and tokens:
  - X-Idempotency-Key: opaque client-supplied key (UUID v4 recommended).
  - X-Idemp-Version: semantic version string (e.g., "1").
  - X-Resume-Token: server-issued opaque token present in each stream chunk metadata; used by SDK to request resume at a later offset. Token encodes (signed) replica-id, sequence-offset, model-version, and token-expiry; clients do not parse it.
  - Resume requests must include the original X-Idempotency-Key and the last-seen X-Resume-Token.
- Server semantics:
  - On initial request: accept X-Idempotency-Key if provided; return resume_tokens in stream metadata periodically (every N messages or bytes).
  - On resume request: verify idempotency key ownership and model-version compatibility. If the new serving replica can deterministically reconstruct the remainder of the stream from the provided resume_token, it returns a 200 and resumes; otherwise it returns 409 (cannot resume) and the client restarts the request.
  - For MUTATING endpoints: server must ensure side-effect deduplication by consulting an idempotency ledger keyed by X-Idempotency-Key before applying any final commit. Resume flows must be no-op if commit already observed.
- Hedged requests interaction:
  - SDK hedging should not issue simultaneous resume attempts to multiple regions for the same resume_token. Hedge policy: primary tries resume first; if primary fails timeout T_resume, issue single hedged resume to fallback region. Hedge window is smaller than initial request hedging to avoid duplicate commits.
- Circuit breakers & load shedding:
  - Resume attempts evaluate failure budgets; if region is in CircuitOpen for resume traffic, SDK should fall back to full-restart or surface transient error depending on endpoint classification.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec document published and reviewed by Platform and SDK leads.
- Runtime implements opaque resume_token issuance and verification in staging for a single model family.
- JS and Python SDKs add resume primitive: Stream.resume(resumeToken) plus automatic resume on transient network error when X-Idempotency-Key present.
- Integration test harness that simulates region failover and proves no duplicate commits for MUTATING endpoints in 10/10 runs.
- Dashboard showing resume success rate, resume-induced duplicates (should be zero for mutating endpoints), and resume latency.

Migration plan and rollout:
1) Spec + SDK shim (non-breaking): servers start including X-Resume-Token in streams; SDKs ignore until upgraded. (2 weeks)
2) SDK patch release (minor): adds resume primitives and optional auto-resume behind a feature flag. (1 week)
3) Enable auto-resume for internal customers and beta partners; collect metrics. (2 weeks)
4) Server-side enforcement for MUTATING endpoints: require X-Idempotency-Key when auto-resume is on; return 412 if missing. (1 week)
5) Gradual global rollout with circuit-breaker thresholds and toggleable hedging parameters. (2 weeks)

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: resume_token_issued, resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_conflict_409, resume_fallback_restarts, resume_duplicate_commits_detected.
- Dashboards: Resume Health (per-region), Resume Latency SLO, Resume Conflict Rate. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/resume-health (placeholder).
- Alerts: resume_conflict_409_rate > 1% over 5m for MUTATING endpoints.

Security considerations:
- Resume tokens are opaque signed blobs; rotate signing keys quarterly and include key-id in token metadata.
- Resume_token expiry default 15 minutes to limit replay risk.
- Security review required to confirm ledger access controls and resume_token signing.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for resume token generation and verification, including cross-version model mismatches.
- Fault-injection harness that kills primary region mid-stream and confirms resume path works across regions.
- Property tests to ensure idempotency ledger prevents duplicates for mutating endpoints.

Rollout rollback plan:
- If resume_conflict_409 spikes or duplicate_commits detected, disable auto-resume feature flag globally and revert to SDKs ignoring X-Resume-Token. Servers keep issuing tokens but do not rely on them.

Links and artifacts:
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INF/Streaming+Resume+Protocol (draft)
- SDK PR (JS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1298
- SDK PR (Python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/724
- Runtime PR (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2046
- Incident context (prod outage 2026-01-18): https://incident.redwood.example/2026-01-18-streaming-failover

Open questions:
- Resume token expiry window: 15m vs 1h tradeoffs (shorter reduces replay risk, longer helps slow client resumes).
- How to surface resume failures to end-users vs just telemetry.
- Ledger storage strategy for high-volume short-lived idempotency keys (LRU vs TTL-backed store).

Next steps:
- Technical review session with SDK and Runtime (scheduled 2026-02-18).
- Prototype runtime resume token in staging by 2026-02-28.
- Cut experimental SDK release with feature flag by 2026-03-07.
